executive_summary.company_overview: Thermify installs immersion-cooled compute clusters (HeatHubs) in domestic homes, running cloud workloads for business clients while capturing waste heat to replace gas boilers — using energy twice for both computation and home heating. The company is at TRL 7-8 with a live pilot (SHIELD project with UK Power Networks in Essex), Welsh Government backing, and a production facility at Sony's Pencoed site in South Wales.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Waste heat recovery from IT/edge compute infrastructure, domestic heating decarbonisation, fuel poverty alleviation, and distributed low-carbon energy systems are all strongly represented in current UK and EU funding landscapes. The convergence of data centre sustainability and building heat decarbonisation is an emerging priority across Innovate UK, Horizon Europe, and Ofgem innovation programmes.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: The UK is the primary funding landscape given Thermify's operational base, Welsh Government relationship, and existing SHIELD partnership with UK Power Networks. EU Horizon Europe is a strong secondary geography given UK association status and the existence of a call (CL5-2027) that is an almost exact description of Thermify's technology.
executive_summary.key_constraints: Thermify's TRL 7-8 stage means it is too advanced for early-stage research calls (e.g. ARIA's typical focus) but may not yet have the commercial scale evidence required for the largest deployment grants. The Ofgem SIF — arguably the best structural fit — requires a licensed network operator as lead applicant, meaning Thermify must work through UK Power Networks or a similar partner. EU Horizon calls require consortium formation and are complex to navigate as a seed-stage SME.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue Welsh SMART FIS immediately as a low-friction, high-probability near-term grant given existing Welsh Government relationships. Simultaneously prepare for the Horizon Europe CL5-2027 call (exact technology match) by building a consortium now. Use the SHIELD/UK Power Networks relationship to position for Ofgem SIF Cycle 6 as a named technology partner. Apply to EIC Accelerator for transformational upside.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: United Kingdom (primary — existing relationships, Welsh base, SHIELD pilot) and EU/Horizon Europe (secondary — exact thematic call exists for 2027).
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: 1) Welsh SMART FIS (open now, direct, low burden); 2) Horizon Europe CL5-2027 (exact match, begin consortium building now for 2027 deadline); 3) Ofgem SIF via UK Power Networks as lead partner; 4) EIC Accelerator for scale-up capital.
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: UK Power Networks (already engaged via SHIELD — ideal Ofgem SIF lead applicant); a UK university engineering/computer science department (unlocks KTP and strengthens Horizon bids); a European research institute or university (required for Horizon Europe consortium); Welsh Government/Business Wales (existing relationship, strengthens SMART FIS and regional credibility).
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: Thermify needs to build a stronger commercial revenue evidence base (cloud business client contracts) to satisfy EIC Accelerator's market traction requirements. For Horizon Europe, the company needs an established EU consortium partner. For larger Innovate UK deployment grants, documented carbon savings data from the SHIELD pilot will be critical.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: 1) Ofgem SIF partner dependency — UK Power Networks must agree to lead; 2) EIC Accelerator's <5% success rate makes it a long shot without significant preparation; 3) Horizon Europe consortium formation is time-consuming for a seed-stage team; 4) Programme umbrella grants (Net Zero Heat, Industrial Strategy) have no confirmed open rounds, creating pipeline uncertainty.

opportunities.name: EIC Accelerator Open 2026
opportunities.geography: EU member states + associated countries (UK eligible)

opportunities.strategic_value_explanation: EIC Accelerator backing is one of the most powerful credibility signals available to a European deeptech startup, opening doors to EU institutional investors, corporate partners, and follow-on funding at scale.

opportunities.reason_for_caution: The sub-5% success rate and multi-stage process make this a significant time investment with low probability of success — only pursue if the team can dedicate substantial capacity or engage a specialist EIC application consultant.

company_profile.name: Thermify
company_profile.value_proposition: Thermify replaces domestic gas boilers with a compact in-home data centre (HeatHub) that runs cloud computing workloads for business clients while capturing the waste heat to warm homes and heat hot water — eliminating the need for separate cooling infrastructure and reducing household energy bills.
company_profile.technology: Immersion-cooled Raspberry Pi compute clusters (HeatHub units) installed in domestic homes; waste heat from cloud compute workloads is transferred directly into the home's central heating system, effectively using energy twice — once for computation and once for heating. Cloud computing services are sold to business clients (Thermify Cloud for Business) to fund and sustain the model.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Reduction in household carbon emissions and energy bills by replacing gas boilers with waste-heat-recovering compute nodes, while simultaneously reducing data centre cooling energy consumption.
secondary_benefits: Affordable low-carbon heating for low-income and fuel-poor households
Elimination of separate data centre cooling energy overhead
Scalable distributed cloud infrastructure with positive environmental impact
Support for net zero transition in social housing
company_profile.hq: Wales, United Kingdom (facility at Sony's Pencoed site, South Wales; also referenced in London)
company_profile.trl: TRL 7-8 — technology has been demonstrated in real home environments (e.g. BBC-covered Essex pilot with documented bill reductions from £375 to £40/month); SHIELD project partnership with UK Power Networks deploying units in low-income households in Essex; production and assembly capability being built out in Wales.
company_profile.website_summary: Thermify installs small, immersion-cooled data centre units (HeatHubs) inside domestic homes, running cloud computing workloads for business clients and capturing the resulting heat to replace gas boilers for home heating and hot water. The model uses energy twice — once for computation and once for warmth — removing the need for traditional data centre cooling. The company targets both commercial cloud customers and vulnerable or low-income households seeking affordable, low-carbon heating.
company_profile.external_findings: Thermify has secured a notable pilot partnership with UK Power Networks through the SHIELD project (Smart Heat and Intelligent Energy in Low-income Districts), deploying HeatHub units alongside solar panels and battery storage in Essex homes, with documented household energy bill reductions from ~£375 to ~£40 per month. The company has received Welsh Government backing and is establishing a production and assembly facility at Sony's Pencoed site in South Wales, led by CEO Travis Theune, a Silicon Valley entrepreneur with 25+ years of data centre experience. Thermify has run an EIS-eligible crowdfunding raise on Seedrs (Republic Europe) to grow its cloud team, expand marketing, and scale manufacturing.

acronym_definitions.definition: Advanced Research and Invention Agency — UK public funding body established to support unconventional, high-risk research and invention
European Innovation Council — EU body that funds breakthrough innovations and deep-tech startups through grants and equity investment
European Union — supranational political and economic union whose institutions manage programmes such as Horizon Europe and the EIC
Flexible Innovation Support — Welsh Government grant scheme supporting SME innovation and R&D delivered through Business Wales
Intellectual Property — legally protected innovations, designs, or knowledge assets relevant to grant eligibility and commercialisation plans
Knowledge Transfer Partnership — Innovate UK programme funding collaboration between a business and a UK university to embed specialist research capability
Research and Development — activities that qualify for innovation grant funding under most national and EU programmes
Welsh Government innovation grant brand (SMART Flexible Innovation Support) — programme funding SME research, development, and innovation in Wales
Small and Medium-sized Enterprise — company category used to determine eligibility for many grant programmes
Technology Readiness Level — scale from 1–9 measuring the maturity of a technology, used by funders to define eligibility
United Kingdom — sovereign state eligible for certain EU funding programmes under Horizon Europe association agreements
UK Research and Innovation — umbrella body overseeing UK public research and innovation funding, including Innovate UK
